name: PA-14
label: Safe R

key_factors: District leans R+17, among the most Republican in Pennsylvania
Reschenthaler holds a roughly 11-to-1 fundraising advantage
Prediction markets price the Democrat at about 3 percent
No polls, expert ratings, or outside spending signal competitiveness
model.rationale: The district's 17-point Republican lean, the incumbent's dominant fundraising edge, and markets pricing the Democrat near 3 percent all point to a safe Republican hold; even a national environment tilted toward Democrats leaves a large gap to close, and no polling or spending activity suggests the race is in play.
model.watch: A late wave of Democratic outside spending or an unexpected scandal involving the incumbent could narrow the margin, though nothing currently points in that direction.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Southwestern Pennsylvania's 14th District leans heavily Republican, with a partisan lean of roughly 17 points toward the GOP, and incumbent Guy Reschenthaler is seeking another term. He has raised about $4.2 million and holds nearly $1 million on hand, while Democrat Alan Bradstock has raised about $370,000 with $64,000 available. No outside groups are spending meaningfully on either side, and no public polls of the race are available.

Prediction markets give the Democrat roughly a 3 percent chance of winning, and no expert raters flag the contest as competitive. Even with a national environment that favors Democrats by several points, the district's underlying lean, the incumbent's financial advantage, and the absence of polling or spending activity all point to a comfortable Republican hold. The main question is the size of the margin, not the winner.
